propositions: On the agentic execution path, the accumulated tool-result message history is re-sent uncached every turn, causing O(N^2) input token cost growth over multi-turn runs.
The cache_settings_for function sets only 2 of 4 available cache breakpoints (system and tool definitions) but omits message-tail caching, leaving only the static prefix cacheable.
Rebar's telemetry cannot detect this inefficiency because warn_if_cache_ineffective requires cache_read_tokens==0 to fire, but system-block cache reads mask the uncached message tail.

Anthropic and Bedrock expose different cache control keys (anthropic_cache vs bedrock_cache_messages), and Bedrock rejects top-level cache_control directives outright, requiring provider-specific implementations.
Multi-turn agentic runs with N tool results re-send ~N*(N-1)/2 tokens uncached at message breakpoints where caching support already exists in the pinned pydantic-ai dependency.
